subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should legacy session rows without `pluginOwnerId` remain outside plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` authority, or receive a migration or explicit adoption path?
rationale: The branch deliberately chooses a fail-closed authorization policy for persisted legacy state; code inspection cannot determine the intended security and upgrade contract.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed
options.body: Treat ownerless rows as non-plugin-owned and document an operator or doctor recovery path for legitimate legacy plugin sessions.

options.title: Migrate Proven Owners
options.body: Stamp `pluginOwnerId` only where a dedicated migration can establish the owning plugin safely.

options.title: Add Explicit Adoption
options.body: Define a separately authorized one-time adoption operation rather than allowing ordinary patch calls to claim ownership.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Treat ownerless rows as non-plugin-owned and document an operator or doctor recovery path for legitimate legacy plugin sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest verified adjacent history in the same session lifecycle mutation handler and test surface.
